pages.description: Calculations evaluated in another symbol or timeframe.
pages.intro: A request evaluates an expression in a child context fed by its own data stream. Requests explains binding and synchronization in depth.

entries.summary: Evaluates an expression on another symbol’s or timeframe’s data and returns its value for each bar.
signatures:
request.security(
    symbol: string,
    timeframe: string,
    expression: any value,
    fill?: string
) → request-dependent result

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: The symbol of the requested data, recorded for the host, which binds the matching data stream. It must be known when the script is bound: a constant, an input, or a fixed value such as [`syminfo.tickerid`](#syminfo.tickerid). Cannot be `na`.

parameters.name: timeframe
parameters.description: The timeframe of the requested data, such as `"60"` (60 minutes) or `"D"` (one day). Like `symbol`, it must be known when the script is bound. Cannot be `na`.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: The calculation to run on the requested data, with that data’s own bars and history. It must produce one `int`, `float`, `bool`, `string`, `color` or enum value. It may read the script’s constants and inputs, except source inputs, but no other script variables; call a function to use several statements. Evaluated in the requested context.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: What the result holds on a bar where no new requested value arrived since the previous bar: `"carry"`, the default, repeats the latest value, and `"sparse"` gives `na`. It must be known when the script is bound. Cannot be `na`.

entries.returns: The expression’s value from the requested data for the current bar, with the expression’s type; the type’s empty value (`na`, or `false` for `bool`) until the requested data has produced a value.
entries.body:
The call must be the entire initializer of a top-level variable, such as `daily = request.security(...)`. The host binds the requested data stream under that variable’s name; Tea fetches no data itself. When both data streams carry event times, each bar receives the newest requested value that opened at or before it; otherwise requested values are paired with bars in order. History inside `expression` refers to the requested data, so `close[1]` there is its previous bar. Inside `expression`, `syminfo` and `timeframe` values are what the host supplies for the requested data; Tea does not set them from `symbol` and `timeframe`. To get several values, declare one request for each. See Requests for binding and synchronization.

```tea
daily = request.security(syminfo.tickerid, "D", close[1])
emit "previous_daily_close" daily
```

entries.summary: Collects an expression’s values from finer-grained data into an array for each bar.
signatures:
request.security_lower_tf(
    symbol: string,
    timeframe: string,
    expression: any value
) → request-dependent result

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: The symbol of the requested data, recorded for the host, which binds the matching data stream. It must be known when the script is bound: a constant, an input, or a fixed value such as [`syminfo.tickerid`](#syminfo.tickerid). Cannot be `na`.

parameters.name: timeframe
parameters.description: The timeframe of the requested data, such as `"60"` (60 minutes) or `"D"` (one day). Like `symbol`, it must be known when the script is bound. Cannot be `na`.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: The calculation to run on the requested data, with that data’s own bars and history. It must produce one `int`, `float`, `bool`, `string`, `color` or enum value. It may read the script’s constants and inputs, except source inputs, but no other script variables; call a function to use several statements. Evaluated in the requested context.

entries.returns: An array of the expression’s values that belong to the current bar, oldest first; empty when there are none.
entries.body:
The call must be the entire initializer of a top-level variable, such as `ranges = request.security_lower_tf(...)`. The host binds the requested data stream under that variable’s name; Tea fetches no data itself. When both data streams carry event times, a bar collects the requested values that opened after the previous bar and up to its own time. Without event times, a bar collects a fixed number of values when both streams have regular periods that divide evenly, and one value otherwise. Inside `expression`, `syminfo` and `timeframe` values are what the host supplies for the requested data; Tea does not set them from `symbol` and `timeframe`. See Requests.

```tea
ranges = request.security_lower_tf(syminfo.tickerid, "15", high - low)
emit "intraday_bars" ranges.size()
```

pages.title: Market data
pages.description: Prices, bar and time values, symbol and timeframe information, and bar state.
pages.intro:
Values the host supplies for the current bar, available in every script without an import. Each entry says what it holds inside a request.

Price and volume of the current row, read from input columns the host supplies.

Each name reads the input column of the same name, as [`close`](#close)
describes. The host must supply every column a script reads, or binding the
script fails. Library files can read these names too, and no file can
redeclare or assign them.

Available in every script without an import or namespace.

entries.summary: Opening price of the current row.
entries.body: Reads the host-supplied `open` column, like [`close`](#close).

entries.summary: Highest price of the current row.
entries.body: Reads the host-supplied `high` column, like [`close`](#close).

entries.summary: Lowest price of the current row.
entries.body: Reads the host-supplied `low` column, like [`close`](#close).

entries.summary: Closing price of the current row.
entries.body:
Reads the `close` column of the host's input stream. A row is one item of
that stream, such as one bar, and `close` is `na` on a row where the host
supplies `NaN`. Inside a request expression, it reads the
stream bound to that request instead.

`close[1]` is the value one row earlier and is `na` on the first row. This
computes the change from the previous row, using [`nz`](#nz) to treat the
missing first value as no change:

```tea
previous = nz(close[1], close)
emit "change" close - previous
```

entries.summary: Traded volume of the current row.
entries.body: Reads the host-supplied `volume` column, like [`close`](#close).

entries.summary: Midpoint of the current row's high and low, `(high + low) / 2`.
entries.body:
Tea does not compute it: it reads the host-supplied `hl2` column, like
[`close`](#close). `tea run` derives that column from `high` and `low` when the
CSV file lacks it.

entries.summary: Average of the current row's high, low and close, `(high + low + close) / 3`.
entries.body:
Tea does not compute it: it reads the host-supplied `hlc3` column, like
[`close`](#close). `tea run` derives that column from `high`, `low` and `close`
when the CSV file lacks it.

entries.summary: Average of the current row's open, high, low and close, `(open + high + low + close) / 4`.
entries.body:
Tea does not compute it: it reads the host-supplied `ohlc4` column, like
[`close`](#close). `tea run` derives that column from `open`, `high`, `low` and
`close` when the CSV file lacks it.

entries.summary: Average of the current row's high, low and doubled close, `(high + low + 2 * close) / 4`.
entries.body:
Tea does not compute it: it reads the host-supplied `hlcc4` column, like
[`close`](#close). `tea run` derives that column from `high`, `low` and `close`
when the CSV file lacks it.

entries.summary: The number of the current bar, counting from 0.
entries.body: It grows by one each time a bar is finalized; repeated updates of a live bar keep the same number. Inside a request expression it counts the requested data’s bars.

entries.summary: The current bar’s time, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
entries.body: It is the `time` field of the current input row, the time at which the bar opens. Reading it requires the bound data stream to carry that field; without it, the run stops with an error. Inside a request expression it is the requested data’s bar time.

entries.summary: The current clock time, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
entries.body: The host’s clock is read once for each execution, so repeated updates of a live bar can see different values. A host may supply a fixed clock instead, for reproducible runs. Inside a request expression it is read when the requested data’s bar executes.

entries.summary: The full symbol identifier, including its exchange prefix, such as `NASDAQ:AAPL`.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script; `na` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data, not the request’s `symbol`.

entries.summary: The symbol name without its exchange prefix, such as `AAPL` for `NASDAQ:AAPL`.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script; `na` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data, not the request’s `symbol`.

entries.summary: The exchange prefix of the symbol, such as `NASDAQ` for `NASDAQ:AAPL`.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script; `na` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data, not the request’s `symbol`.

entries.summary: The currency the symbol’s prices are quoted in, such as `USD`.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script; `na` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data, not the request’s `symbol`.

entries.summary: The base currency of a currency pair, such as `BTC` for `BTCUSD`.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script; `na` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data, not the request’s `symbol`.

entries.summary: The kind of instrument, such as `stock` or `crypto`.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script; `na` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data, not the request’s `symbol`.

entries.summary: The time zone of the symbol’s exchange, such as `America/New_York`.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script; `na` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data, not the request’s `symbol`.

entries.summary: The smallest price increment of the symbol.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script; `na` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data, not the request’s `symbol`.

entries.summary: The value of a one-point price move, in the symbol’s currency.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script; `na` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data, not the request’s `symbol`.

entries.summary: The timeframe of the script’s data as text, such as `"15"` or `"D"`.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script; `na` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data, not the request’s `timeframe`.

entries.summary: The number of units in the timeframe, such as `15` for a 15-minute timeframe.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script; `na` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data, not the request’s `timeframe`.

entries.summary: Whether the timeframe is measured in seconds.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script, separately from [`timeframe.period`](#timeframe.period); `false` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data.

entries.summary: Whether the timeframe is measured in minutes.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script, separately from [`timeframe.period`](#timeframe.period); `false` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data.

entries.summary: Whether the timeframe is shorter than one day.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script, separately from [`timeframe.period`](#timeframe.period); `false` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data.

entries.summary: Whether the timeframe is measured in days.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script, separately from [`timeframe.period`](#timeframe.period); `false` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data.

entries.summary: Whether the timeframe is measured in weeks.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script, separately from [`timeframe.period`](#timeframe.period); `false` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data.

entries.summary: Whether the timeframe is measured in months.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script, separately from [`timeframe.period`](#timeframe.period); `false` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data.

entries.summary: Whether the timeframe is measured in days, weeks or months.
entries.body: Supplied by the host when it binds the script, separately from [`timeframe.period`](#timeframe.period); `false` when the host supplies none. Inside a request expression it is the host’s value for the requested data.

entries.summary: Whether the current bar is the first one, where [`bar_index`](#bar_index) is 0.
entries.body: Inside a request expression it refers to the requested data’s first bar.

entries.summary: Whether the script is processing historical data.
entries.body: It is always the opposite of [`barstate.isrealtime`](#barstate.isrealtime), including inside a request expression.

entries.summary: Whether the script is processing live data.
entries.body: The host reports it for each execution. It is `false` unless the host marks the data as live, so runs over stored data report `false`. Inside a request expression it is read when the requested data’s bar executes.

entries.summary: Whether the current update is the bar’s final one.
entries.body:
It is `false` on provisional updates of a live bar and `true` on its final update. Rows that are not marked provisional are final, so historical bars are always confirmed. Inside a request expression it describes the requested data’s update. Use it to act only on completed bars.

```tea
var int completed = 0
if barstate.isconfirmed
    completed := completed + 1
emit "completed_bars" completed
```

entries.summary: Whether this is the first update of the current bar.
entries.body: It is `true` for the first execution of each bar and `false` when a live bar is updated again. Historical bars run once, so they are always new. Inside a request expression it describes the requested data’s bar.

pages.title: Plots and alerts
pages.description: Named chart outputs, alerts and their style constants.
pages.intro:
Each call writes one named output that a host can draw or deliver. See outputs and events.

Functions that describe plots, shapes, colors and alerts as named outputs.

Each call records its arguments in a description value and writes it to the
output named by its first argument, `id`. Tea draws and sends nothing: the
host decides how to draw or deliver each output, so options such as
`linewidth` or `display` are hints recorded exactly as passed. Only the
script itself can call these functions, not a library file.

An `id` is a constant string, unique among the script's outputs; only alert
calls may share one. It cannot be empty or one of `index`, `time`, `timed`
and `provisional`. Apart from the alerts, a call may run at most once per
row, so not inside a loop, and on a row where it does not run, such as
inside an `if` whose condition is false, its output holds no value.

Available in every script without an import or namespace.

entries.summary: Writes one value per row, with options for drawing it, to a named output.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Name of the output this call writes.

parameters.name: series
parameters.description: Value to plot on the current row; may be `na`.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Display name, separate from `id`.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Color on the current row, such as [`color.red`](#color.*); it may change from row to row. `na` records no color, leaving the choice to the host.

parameters.name: linewidth
parameters.description: Width of the line.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: How to draw the values: a `plot.style_*` constant such as [`plot.style_line`](#plot.style_*), [`plot.style_histogram`](#plot.style_*) or [`plot.style_columns`](#plot.style_*).

parameters.name: trackprice
parameters.description: Whether to also mark the latest value with a horizontal price line.

parameters.name: histbase
parameters.description: Base level for the histogram, column and area styles.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of rows to shift the drawing by.

parameters.name: editable
parameters.description: Whether users may edit the output's style in the host.

parameters.name: show_last
parameters.description: How many of the most recent rows to draw.

parameters.name: display
parameters.description: Where the output appears: a `display.*` constant such as [`display.all`](#display.*) or [`display.none`](#display.*).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Number format: [`format.inherit`](#format.*), [`format.price`](#format.*), [`format.volume`](#format.*) or [`format.percent`](#format.*).

parameters.name: precision
parameters.description: Number of decimal places to show.

entries.returns: The description written to `id`. Its fields hold the arguments under the parameter names, such as `series` and `color`; pass it to [`fill`](#fill) to shade between two plots.
entries.body:
This plots a 20-row average, green while the close is above it:

```tea
average = ta.sma(close, 20)
plot("average", average, "SMA 20", color=close > average ? color.green : color.red, linewidth=2)
```

entries.summary: Writes a horizontal line at a fixed level to a named output.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Name of the output this call writes.

parameters.name: price
parameters.description: Level of the line. It can come from an input but cannot change from row to row.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Display name, separate from `id`.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Line color; like `price`, it cannot change from row to row. `na` records no color, leaving the choice to the host.

parameters.name: linestyle
parameters.description: Line style: [`hline.style_solid`](#hline.style_*), [`hline.style_dotted`](#hline.style_*) or [`hline.style_dashed`](#hline.style_*).

parameters.name: linewidth
parameters.description: Width of the line.

parameters.name: editable
parameters.description: Whether users may edit the output's style in the host.

parameters.name: display
parameters.description: Where the output appears: a `display.*` constant such as [`display.all`](#display.*) or [`display.none`](#display.*).

entries.returns: The description written to `id`, with fields named after the parameters; pass it to [`fill`](#fill) to shade between two lines.

entries.summary: Writes a shaded area between two plots or horizontal lines to a named output.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Name of the output this call writes.

parameters.name: plot1
parameters.description: One edge of the area: the value returned by [`plot`](#plot) or [`hline`](#hline). Only its `id` is recorded.

parameters.name: plot2
parameters.description: The other edge, given like `plot1`.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Fill color on the current row; it may change from row to row. `na` records no color, leaving the choice to the host.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Display name, separate from `id`.

parameters.name: editable
parameters.description: Whether users may edit the output's style in the host.

parameters.name: display
parameters.description: Where the output appears: a `display.*` constant such as [`display.all`](#display.*) or [`display.none`](#display.*).

entries.returns: The description written to `id`; its `first` and `second` fields hold the IDs of `plot1` and `plot2`.
entries.body:
The description refers to the two outputs by their IDs. This shades the area
between a fast and a slow average:

```tea
fast = plot("fast", ta.ema(close, 10), "Fast EMA", color=color.blue)
slow = plot("slow", ta.ema(close, 30), "Slow EMA", color=color.orange)
fill("band", fast, slow, color=color.new(color.blue, 80))
```

entries.summary: Writes a shape marker for the rows where a condition is true to a named output.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Name of the output this call writes.

parameters.name: series
parameters.description: Whether the shape appears on the current row.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Display name, separate from `id`.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: Shape to draw: a `shape.*` constant such as [`shape.circle`](#shape.*), [`shape.triangleup`](#shape.*) or [`shape.xcross`](#shape.*).

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Where to place the shape: a `location.*` constant such as [`location.abovebar`](#location.*) or [`location.belowbar`](#location.*).

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Shape color on the current row; `na` records no color, leaving the choice to the host.

parameters.name: offset

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Text to show with the shape.

parameters.name: textcolor
parameters.description: Color of `text` on the current row; `na` records no color, leaving the choice to the host.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Shape size: a `size.*` constant such as [`size.auto`](#size.*), [`size.small`](#size.*) or [`size.large`](#size.*).

parameters.name: editable
parameters.description: Whether users may edit the output's style in the host.

parameters.name: show_last
parameters.description: How many of the most recent rows to draw.

parameters.name: display
parameters.description: Where the output appears: a `display.*` constant such as [`display.all`](#display.*) or [`display.none`](#display.*).

entries.returns: The description written to `id`, with fields named after the parameters.
entries.body:
The description is written on every row the call runs; its `series` field
records whether the shape appears on that row. This marks each row where the
close crosses above its 20-row average:

```tea
crossed = ta.crossover(close, ta.sma(close, 20))
plotshape("cross", crossed, "Cross", style=shape.triangleup, location=location.belowbar, color=color.green)
```

This tints the rows where the close is above its 50-row average and records
no color for the others:


parameters.name: id

parameters.name: color

entries.summary: Appends an alert event with fixed text on each row where a condition is true.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Name of the event list this call appends to. Several `alertcondition` calls may share one `id`; their events keep the order in which the calls run.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: Whether to append an event on the current row.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Event title.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Event message.

entries.returns: Nothing; use the call as a statement.
entries.body:
Each such row appends one event with the fields `title` and `message`; other
rows append nothing. A condition that stays true appends an event on every
row, so pass a transition such as [`ta.crossover`](#ta.crossover) to alert once per
crossing. When the host re-runs the current row with live updates, each run
replaces that row's events; combine the condition with
[`barstate.isconfirmed`](#barstate.isconfirmed) to append only on the row's final run. Tea
sends no notification: the host decides what to do with each event.

```tea
crossed = ta.crossover(close, ta.sma(close, 20))
alertcondition("cross", barstate.isconfirmed and crossed, "Cross", "Close crossed its 20-row average")
```

entries.summary: Appends an alert event with per-row text and a struct payload on each row where a condition is true.
signatures:
alert(
    const string id,
    series bool condition,
    series string title,
    series string message,
    data,
)

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Name of the event list this call appends to. Several `alert` calls may share one `id` when they pass the same `data` type; an `alertcondition` call cannot share it.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: Whether to append an event on the current row.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Event title; may change from row to row.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Event message; may change from row to row.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Payload: any struct value, such as `Move.new(syminfo.ticker, close)`. Numbers, arrays and other non-struct values are rejected.

entries.returns: Nothing; use the call as a statement.
entries.body:
Each row where `condition` is true appends one event with the fields
`title`, `message` and `data`; other rows append nothing. Unlike
[`alertcondition`](#alertcondition), the text can change from row to row, and `data`
carries a struct value whose fields keep their types in the output. Repeated
true rows and live re-runs behave as for [`alertcondition`](#alertcondition).

```tea
struct Move
    string symbol
    float price

alert("move", barstate.isconfirmed and close > 50, "Price above 50", "Close " + str.tostring(close), Move.new(syminfo.ticker, close))
```

entries.summary: Drawing styles for the `style` argument of [`plot`](#plot).

rows: A line through the values that bridges `na` values.
Horizontal steps that change level at each new value.
A vertical bar from the `histbase` level to each value.
A filled column from the `histbase` level to each value.
A line with the area between it and the `histbase` level filled.
Like `plot.style_line`, but with a gap wherever the value is `na`.
Like `plot.style_area`, but with a gap wherever the value is `na`.

Each constant is a `const string`.

pages.title: ta
pages.description: Technical-analysis functions written in Tea.
pages.intro:
Technical-analysis functions: moving averages, oscillators, volatility bands, crosses and running statistics.

Each written call keeps its own history and state, covering only the bars on
which that call runs. Call these functions on every bar and combine their
results with conditions afterwards: a call inside an `if` branch, one arm of a
ternary, or after `and` or `or` does not run when that code is skipped, so its
window reads the skipped bars as `na` and its running state does not change on
them. A call inside a loop shares one history and state across all iterations.
See values and control flow.

Most results are `na` until enough bars have arrived; each entry states when.
The time-series guide covers warm-up and
crossing rules.

```tea
// Call on every bar, then combine the result with the condition.
risingThree = ta.rising(close, 3)
emit "signal" close > open and risingThree
```

Available in every script as `ta.name` without an import.

entries.summary: Simple moving average of the last `length` values of `source`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to average, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The mean; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars and while any value in the window is `na`.

entries.summary: Exponential moving average of `source`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to average, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Smoothing length in bars; larger values react more slowly.

entries.returns: The average; `na` before the first value of `source` and on bars where `source` is `na`.
entries.body:
Each bar moves the average toward `source` by `2 / (length + 1)` of the
difference. It starts from the first value of `source` instead of waiting for
`length` bars. An `na` value restarts it: the result is `na` on that bar, and
the average starts over from the next value. Compare [`ta.rma`](#ta.rma), which
waits for `length` values and skips `na`.

entries.summary: Wilder's moving average of `source`, the smoothing behind [`ta.rsi`](#ta.rsi), [`ta.atr`](#ta.atr) and [`ta.dmi`](#ta.dmi).

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to average.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Smoothing length in bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The average; `na` until `length` values that are not `na` have arrived.
entries.body:
It starts as the simple average of the first `length` values that are not
`na`, then moves toward each new value by `1 / length` of the difference. An
`na` value is skipped: it does not count toward the first `length` values,
and later the previous result is kept.

entries.summary: Linearly weighted moving average of the last `length` values of `source`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to average, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The weighted mean; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars and while any value in the window is `na`.
entries.body:
The newest value has weight `length`, the one before it `length - 1`, and so
on down to `1` for the oldest.

entries.summary: Volume-weighted moving average of the last `length` values of `source`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to average, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The weighted mean; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars, while any price or volume in the window is `na`, and when the window's total volume is `0`.
entries.body:
It is `ta.sma(source * volume, length) / ta.sma(volume, length)`, weighting
each bar by its [`volume`](#volume).

entries.summary: Hull moving average of `source`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to average, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, an `int` of at least `2`.

entries.returns: The average; `na` for the first `length + math.round(math.sqrt(length)) - 2` bars and while an `na` value of `source` is still inside its windows.
entries.body:
It is the [`ta.wma`](#ta.wma) over `math.round(math.sqrt(length))` bars of
`2 * ta.wma(source, length / 2) - ta.wma(source, length)`, with `length / 2`
rounded down.

entries.summary: Symmetrically weighted moving average of the last four values of `source`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to average, usually [`close`](#close).

entries.returns: The weighted mean; `na` for the first three bars and while any of the four values is `na`.
entries.body:
The weights are `1/6`, `2/6`, `2/6` and `1/6`, from the oldest value to the
newest.

entries.summary: Arnaud Legoux moving average: a bell-curve-weighted average of the last `length` values of `source`.
signatures: ta.alma(source, int length, offset, sigma, bool floor = false)

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to average, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Position of the peak weight, from `0` (oldest value) to `1` (newest value).

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.description: Narrowness of the curve; larger values concentrate the weight near the peak.

parameters.name: floor
parameters.description: `true` rounds the peak position down to a whole bar.

entries.returns: The weighted mean; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars and while any value in the window is `na`.
entries.body:
The weights follow a Gaussian curve whose peak sits at `offset` across the
window and whose standard deviation is `length / sigma` bars.

entries.summary: Value of the least-squares line through the last `length` values of `source`, `offset` bars before the current bar.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to fit, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, an `int` of at least `2`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Bars back from the current bar at which to read the line; `0` reads it at the current bar.

entries.returns: The line's value; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars and while any value in the window is `na`.
entries.body:
The line is fitted with the oldest value at position `0` and the current value
at position `length - 1`, then read at position `length - 1 - offset`. A
negative `offset` extends the line past the current bar.

entries.summary: Center of gravity of the last `length` values of `source`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to measure, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The center of gravity; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars, while any value in the window is `na`, and when the values sum to `0`.
entries.body:
It is minus the sum of `source[i] * (i + 1)` divided by the sum of
`source[i]`, for `i` from `0` (the current bar) to `length - 1`, so it is
negative when the values are positive.

entries.summary: Difference between `source` now and `length` bars ago.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to compare.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars back, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: `source - source[length]`; `na` for the first `length` bars and when either value is `na`.

entries.summary: Momentum: `source` minus its value `length` bars ago.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to compare, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars back, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: `source - source[length]`; `na` for the first `length` bars and when either value is `na`.
entries.body: It is the same as [`ta.change`](#ta.change), with `length` required.

entries.summary: Rate of change: the percentage change of `source` from `length` bars ago.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to compare, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars back, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: `100 * (source - source[length]) / source[length]`; `na` for the first `length` bars, when either value is `na`, and when `source[length]` is `0`.

entries.summary: Relative strength index of `source`, from `0` to `100`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to measure, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Smoothing length in bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The index; `na` for the first `length` bars.
entries.body:
Gains and losses from [`ta.change`](#ta.change) are each smoothed with
[`ta.rma`](#ta.rma) over `length` bars, and the result is
`100 - 100 / (1 + gain / loss)`. It is `100` when the smoothed loss is `0`,
including on a flat series, and `0` when the smoothed gain is `0`.

entries.summary: Chande momentum oscillator of `source`, from `-100` to `100`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to measure, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of changes, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The oscillator; `na` for the first `length` bars, while any value in the window is `na`, and when `source` did not change over the window.
entries.body:
Over the last `length` bar-to-bar changes, it is
`100 * (gains - losses) / (gains + losses)`.

entries.summary: True strength index of `source`, from `-1` to `1`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to measure, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: short_length
parameters.description: Length of the second smoothing, in bars.

parameters.name: long_length
parameters.description: Length of the first smoothing, in bars.

entries.returns: The index; `na` on the first bar and until `source` has changed.
entries.body:
The bar-to-bar change of `source` is smoothed twice with [`ta.ema`](#ta.ema),
first over `long_length` bars and then over `short_length` bars, and divided
by the absolute change smoothed the same way.

entries.summary: Stochastic oscillator: where `source` sits between the lowest `l` and highest `h` of the last `length` bars.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to place in the range, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: h
parameters.description: Series whose highest value is the top of the range, usually [`high`](#high).

parameters.name: l
parameters.description: Series whose lowest value is the bottom of the range, usually [`low`](#low).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The percentage; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars, while any value in the windows is `na`, and when the range is `0`.
entries.body:
It is `100 * (source - lowest) / (highest - lowest)`, from `0` to `100` when
`source` lies within that range. The result is not smoothed; pass it to
[`ta.sma`](#ta.sma) to smooth it.

```tea
k = ta.sma(ta.stoch(close, high, low, 14), 3)
d = ta.sma(k, 3)
emit "k" k
emit "d" d
```

entries.summary: Commodity channel index of `source`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to measure, such as [`hlc3`](#hlc3).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The index; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars, while any value in the window is `na`, and when all values in the window are equal.
entries.body:
It is `(source - mean) / (0.015 * deviation)`, where `mean` is the
[`ta.sma`](#ta.sma) and `deviation` the [`ta.dev`](#ta.dev) of the last `length` values.

entries.summary: Williams %R: where [`close`](#close) sits within the range of the last `length` bars, from `-100` to `0`.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The percentage; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars, while any price in the window is `na`, and when the range is `0`.
entries.body:
It is `100 * (close - highest) / (highest - lowest)`, using the highest
[`high`](#high) and the lowest [`low`](#low) of the last `length` bars.

entries.summary: Money flow index of `source`, from `0` to `100`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Price series, usually [`hlc3`](#hlc3).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The index; `0` when bars in the window fell but none rose, and `na` when none fell or the volume of a bar that rose or fell is `na`.
entries.body:
Money flow is `source * volume`, using [`volume`](#volume). Over the last `length`
bars, the flows of bars where `source` rose and of bars where it fell are
summed separately, and the result is `100 - 100 / (1 + rising / falling)`.
Bars whose change cannot be computed, such as the first bar, are left out
instead of making the result `na`.

entries.summary: Moving average convergence divergence of `source`, with its signal line and histogram.
signatures: ta.macd(source, int fastlen, int slowlen, int siglen)

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to measure, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: fastlen
parameters.description: Length of the fast average, in bars.

parameters.name: slowlen
parameters.description: Length of the slow average, in bars.

parameters.name: siglen
parameters.description: Length of the signal line's average, in bars.

entries.returns: A tuple `[macdLine, signalLine, histogram]`, where `histogram` is `macdLine - signalLine`.
entries.body:
The MACD line is `ta.ema(source, fastLength) - ta.ema(source, slowLength)`,
the signal line is its [`ta.ema`](#ta.ema) over `signalLength` bars, and the
histogram is their difference. The averages start from the first value of
`source`, so all three are `0` on the first bar.

```tea
[macdLine, signalLine, histogram] = ta.macd(close, 12, 26, 9)
emit "macd" macdLine
emit "signal" signalLine
emit "histogram" histogram
```

entries.summary: Directional movement index: the +DI and -DI lines and the ADX trend strength, each from `0` to `100`.

parameters.name: diLength
parameters.description: Smoothing length for +DI and -DI, a positive `int`.

parameters.name: adxSmoothing
parameters.description: Smoothing length for ADX, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: A tuple `[plusDI, minusDI, adx]`. +DI and -DI are `na` for the first `diLength - 1` bars, and ADX for the first `diLength + adxSmoothing - 2` bars.
entries.body:
On each bar, the upward move of [`high`](#high) counts toward +DI and the
downward move of [`low`](#low) toward -DI, whichever is larger and positive.
Each is smoothed with [`ta.rma`](#ta.rma) over `diLength` bars and divided by the
true range ([`ta.tr`](#ta.tr)) smoothed the same way. ADX is `100` times the
[`ta.rma`](#ta.rma), over `adxSmoothing` bars, of the absolute difference between
+DI and -DI divided by their sum.

```tea
[plusDI, minusDI, adx] = ta.dmi(14, 14)
emit "+DI" plusDI
emit "-DI" minusDI
emit "ADX" adx
```

entries.summary: True range of the current bar.

parameters.name: handle_na
parameters.description: What to return when the previous [`close`](#close) is `na`, as on the first bar: `true` gives `high - low`, `false` gives `na`.

entries.returns: The true range, or the `handle_na` result when the previous close is `na`.
entries.body:
It is the largest of `high - low`, `math.abs(high - close[1])` and
`math.abs(low - close[1])`, using [`high`](#high), [`low`](#low) and
[`close`](#close).

entries.summary: Average true range: [`ta.tr`](#ta.tr) smoothed with [`ta.rma`](#ta.rma) over `length` bars.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Smoothing length in bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The average; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars.

entries.summary: Mean absolute deviation of the last `length` values of `source` from their average.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to measure.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The deviation; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars and while any value in the window is `na`.

entries.summary: Variance of the last `length` values of `source`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to measure.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

parameters.name: biased
parameters.description: `true` divides by `length` (population variance); `false` divides by `length - 1` (sample variance).

entries.returns: The variance; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars, while any value in the window is `na`, and for a sample variance of one value.

entries.summary: Standard deviation of the last `length` values of `source`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to measure.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

parameters.name: biased
parameters.description: `true` divides by `length` (population); `false` divides by `length - 1` (sample).

entries.returns: The square root of [`ta.variance`](#ta.variance) with the same arguments; `na` whenever that is `na`.

entries.summary: Difference between the highest and lowest of the last `length` values of `source`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to measure.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: The range; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars and while any value in the window is `na`.

entries.summary: Bollinger Bands: the average of `source` with bands `mult` standard deviations above and below it.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to measure, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

parameters.name: mult
parameters.description: Band distance in standard deviations.

entries.returns: A tuple `[middle, upper, lower]`; each is `na` for the first `length - 1` bars and while any value in the window is `na`.
entries.body:
The middle band is the [`ta.sma`](#ta.sma) of the last `length` values, and the
distance is `mult` times their population [`ta.stdev`](#ta.stdev).

```tea
[middle, upper, lower] = ta.bb(close, 20, 2.0)
emit "middle" middle
emit "upper" upper
emit "lower" lower
```

entries.summary: Bollinger Band width as a percentage of the middle band.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to measure, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of bars, a positive `int`.

parameters.name: mult
parameters.description: Band distance in standard deviations.

entries.returns: The width in percent; `na` for the first `length - 1` bars, while any value in the window is `na`, and when the middle band is `0`.
entries.body:
It is `(upper - lower) / middle * 100` for the bands [`ta.bb`](#ta.bb) returns
with the same arguments.

entries.summary: Keltner Channels: an exponential average of `source` with bands `mult` average ranges above and below it.
signatures: ta.kc(source, int length, mult, useTrueRange = true)

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to average, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Smoothing length in bars.

parameters.name: mult
parameters.description: Band distance in average ranges.

parameters.name: useTrueRange
parameters.description: `true` measures each bar's range with `ta.tr(false)`, so the range is `na` on the first bar; `false` uses `high - low`.

entries.returns: A tuple `[middle, upper, lower]`.
entries.body:
The middle line is `ta.ema(source, length)`. The distance is `mult` times the
[`ta.ema`](#ta.ema), over `length` bars, of each bar's [`ta.tr`](#ta.tr), or of
`high - low` when `useTrueRange` is `false`. The averages start on the first
bar, so there is no warm-up `na`.

```tea
[middle, upper, lower] = ta.kc(close, 20, 1.5)
emit "middle" middle
emit "upper" upper
emit "lower" lower
```

entries.summary: Keltner Channel width as a fraction of the middle line.
signatures: ta.kcw(source, int length, mult, useTrueRange = true)

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to average, usually [`close`](#close).

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Smoothing length in bars.

parameters.name: mult
parameters.description: Band distance in average ranges.

parameters.name: useTrueRange
parameters.description: `true` measures each bar's range with [`ta.tr`](#ta.tr); `false` uses `high - low`.

entries.returns: The width as a ratio; `na` when the middle line is `0`.
entries.body:
It is `(upper - lower) / middle` for the channels [`ta.kc`](#ta.kc) returns with
the same arguments. Unlike [`ta.bbw`](#ta.bbw), it is not multiplied by `100`.

entries.summary: Supertrend: a trailing line on one side of price, and the trend direction.

parameters.name: factor
parameters.description: Band distance in average true ranges.

parameters.name: atrPeriod
parameters.description: Length of the [`ta.atr`](#ta.atr), a positive `int`.

entries.returns: A tuple `[line, direction]`. `direction` is `-1` in an uptrend, where `line` is the lower band below price, and `1` in a downtrend, where `line` is the upper band above price; it is `1` until the ATR has a previous value. `line` is `0` on the first bar and `na` until the ATR has a value.
entries.body:
Bands sit `factor` times `ta.atr(atrPeriod)` above and below [`hl2`](#hl2).
The lower band never falls unless the previous [`close`](#close) was below it,
and the upper band never rises unless the previous close was above it. The
trend turns up when `close` rises above the upper band and turns down when
`close` falls below the lower band.

```tea
[line, direction] = ta.supertrend(3.0, 10)
emit "supertrend" line
emit "uptrend" direction == -1
```

entries.summary: Parabolic SAR: a trailing stop that moves faster toward price as the trend makes new extremes.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Initial acceleration factor, such as `0.02`.

parameters.name: inc
parameters.description: Increase of the acceleration factor at each new extreme.

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Largest acceleration factor.

entries.returns: The level; `na` on the first bar, and on every bar if this call did not run on the bar where `bar_index` is `1`.
entries.body:
The trend starts on the bar where [`bar_index`](#bar_index) is `1`: upward with the
level at the previous [`low`](#low) if [`close`](#close) rose, otherwise downward
with the level at the previous [`high`](#high). Each bar the level moves toward
the trend's extreme price by the acceleration factor, which starts at `start`
and grows by `inc`, up to `max`, whenever the trend makes a new extreme. When
the bar's low falls below the level in an uptrend, or its high rises above it
in a downtrend, the trend reverses and the level jumps to the extreme of the
trend that ended. In an uptrend the level stays at or below the previous two
lows; in a downtrend, at or above the previous two highs.

entries.summary: True on the bar where `source1` moves above `source2`.

parameters.name: source1
parameters.description: Series that crosses.

parameters.name: source2
parameters.description: Series or level being crossed.

entries.returns: `true` on the crossing bar, otherwise `false`.
entries.body:
It is `source1 > source2` on this bar and `source1 <= source2` on the
previous bar. Equality on the current bar is not a cross, and a comparison
with `na` is `false`, so the result is `false` on the first bar.

```tea
fast = ta.ema(close, 9)
slow = ta.ema(close, 21)
emit "crossedUp" ta.crossover(fast, slow)
emit "crossedLevel" ta.crossover(close, 100.0)
```

entries.summary: True on the bar where `source1` moves below `source2`.

parameters.name: source1
parameters.description: Series that crosses.

parameters.name: source2
parameters.description: Series or level being crossed.

entries.returns: `true` on the crossing bar, otherwise `false`.
entries.body:
It is `source1 < source2` on this bar and `source1 >= source2` on the
previous bar. Equality on the current bar is not a cross, and the result is
`false` on the first bar.

entries.summary: True on the bar where `source1` crosses `source2` in either direction.

parameters.name: source1
parameters.description: Series that crosses.

parameters.name: source2
parameters.description: Series or level being crossed.

entries.returns: `true` when [`ta.crossover`](#ta.crossover) or [`ta.crossunder`](#ta.crossunder) is `true`, otherwise `false`.

entries.summary: True when `source` rose on each of the last `length` bars.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Series to test.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Number of consecutive rises, a positive `int`.

entries.returns: `true` when every rise happened, otherwise `false`; `false` for the first `length` bars.

pages.title: trade
pages.description: Coordinators that run a strategy's orders through a broker and record the fills in a portfolio.
pages.intro:
Coordinators that run a strategy's orders through a broker and record the fills in a portfolio.

Add `import trade` together with `import broker` and `import portfolio`. A
coordinator owns one broker value and one portfolio value: it submits your
orders to the broker, applies each fill to the portfolio, and refreshes the
account the broker checks before matching continues. Pick the family that
matches how your orders should fill: [`trade.nextOpen`](#trade.nextOpen) (next open, or
this bar's close), [`trade.ohlc`](#trade.ohlc) (anywhere in the bar's range),
[`trade.path`](#trade.path) (along an ordered intrabar path, with trailing exits) or
[`trade.lots`](#trade.lots) (separate lots, executed immediately). The broker
from [`broker.new`](#broker.new) holds one pending order and one attached exit at a
time. Store the coordinator in a `var` so its state persists across bars.
The strategy model describes each lifecycle in detail.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

fast = ta.ema(close, 10)
slow = ta.ema(close, 30)
crossedUp = ta.crossover(fast, slow)
crossedDown = ta.crossunder(fast, slow)

var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.new(), portfolio.new(initialCash = 10000.0))
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if crossedUp and strat.position_quantity() == 0.0
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long)
if crossedDown and strat.position_quantity() > 0.0
    strat.close("Exit")
strat.end_bar(close, false)
plot("equity", strat.snapshot().equity)
```

Add `import trade` to a script to use these as `trade.name`.

entries.summary: Sizes an entry as a percentage of the portfolio's marked equity, read when `entry` is called.
signatures:
trade.percentOfEquity(
    float percent,
    bool commissionIncluded = false
)

parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: Percentage of equity, above `0` and at most `100`.

parameters.name: commissionIncluded
parameters.description: Whether the budget also pays the commission.

entries.returns: A [`trade.Sizing`](#trade.Sizing) for the `sizing` argument of `entry`.
entries.body:
Marked equity comes from the latest `mark` or `end_bar`, or is the initial
cash before the first one. With `commissionIncluded`, the commission is paid
out of the budget; otherwise it is charged on top. If the percentage is not
above `0` and at most `100`, or the marked equity is not positive, the
broker rejects the order when it would fill.

entries.summary: Sizes an entry as a percentage of equity at the moment the order fills.
signatures:
trade.percentOfEquityAtFill(
    float percent,
    bool commissionIncluded = false
)

parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: Percentage of equity, above `0` and at most `100`.

parameters.name: commissionIncluded
parameters.description: Whether the budget also pays the commission.

entries.returns: A [`trade.Sizing`](#trade.Sizing) for the `sizing` argument of `entry`.
entries.body:
The broker values equity as cash plus the position at the matched price
before slippage; when the entry reverses a position, that is after the
closing fill. With `commissionIncluded`, the commission is paid out of the
budget; otherwise it is charged on top. If the percentage is not above `0`
and at most `100`, the broker rejects the order when it would fill.

entries.summary: Creates a coordinator whose orders fill at the next bar's open, or at this bar's close when enabled.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: A broker with the [`broker.NextOpenBroker`](#broker.NextOpenBroker) methods, normally from [`broker.new`](#broker.new).

parameters.name: portfolio
parameters.description: A portfolio with the [`portfolio.NetLedger`](#portfolio.NetLedger) methods, normally from [`portfolio.new`](#portfolio.new).

entries.returns: A [`trade.NextOpenTrade`](#trade.NextOpenTrade) that owns both values.
entries.body:
Each bar, call `begin_bar(open, bar_index)` before your signal logic and
`end_bar(close, false)` after it. With a broker created with
`processOrdersOnClose = true`, `end_bar` also fills orders at the close,
including orders submitted earlier in the same bar. A broker or portfolio
without the required methods is a compile error.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

upper = ta.highest(high, 20)
lower = ta.lowest(low, 20)

var strat = trade.nextOpen(
    broker.new(processOrdersOnClose = true),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 10000.0)
)
strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if close > upper[1] and strat.position_quantity() == 0.0
    strat.entry("Breakout", trade.Direction.long, sizing = trade.percentOfEquity(50.0))
if close < lower[1] and strat.position_quantity() > 0.0
    strat.close("Breakdown")
// processOrdersOnClose lets end_bar fill these orders at this bar's close.
strat.end_bar(close, false)
```

entries.summary: Creates a coordinator that matches orders and one stop/target exit against each bar's high-low range.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: A broker with the [`broker.OhlcBroker`](#broker.OhlcBroker) methods, normally from [`broker.new`](#broker.new).

parameters.name: portfolio
parameters.description: A portfolio with the [`portfolio.NetLedger`](#portfolio.NetLedger) methods, normally from [`portfolio.new`](#portfolio.new).

entries.returns: A [`trade.OhlcTrade`](#trade.OhlcTrade) that owns both values.
entries.body:
Each bar, call `begin_bar(open, high, low, bar_index)`, submit orders and
exits, then call `end_bar(close, false)`. Use [`trade.path`](#trade.path) instead
when the order of the high and low matters or you need trailing exits.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

upper = ta.highest(high, 20)

var strat = trade.ohlc(broker.new(), portfolio.new(initialCash = 10000.0))
strat.begin_bar(open, high, low, bar_index)
if strat.position_quantity() == 0.0 and not na(upper)
    // Resubmitting the same ids each bar moves the pending stop entry and its exit.
    strat.entry("Breakout", trade.Direction.long, qty = 10.0, stop = upper)
    strat.exit("Bracket", fromEntry = "Breakout", stop = upper * 0.95, target = upper * 1.1)
strat.end_bar(close, false)
```

entries.summary: Creates a coordinator that replays each bar as an ordered price path, with fixed and trailing exits.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: A broker with the [`broker.PathBroker`](#broker.PathBroker) methods, normally from [`broker.new`](#broker.new).

parameters.name: portfolio
parameters.description: A portfolio with the [`portfolio.NetLedger`](#portfolio.NetLedger) methods, normally from [`portfolio.new`](#portfolio.new).

entries.returns: A [`trade.PathTrade`](#trade.PathTrade) that owns both values.
entries.body:
Each bar, call `begin_bar(open, high, low, close, bar_index)`, attach or
adjust exits, call `continue_bar(open, high, low, close)`, submit new
orders, then call `end_bar(close, false)`.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

fast = ta.ema(close, 10)
slow = ta.ema(close, 30)
crossedUp = ta.crossover(fast, slow)

var strat = trade.path(broker.new(), portfolio.new(initialCash = 10000.0))
fills = strat.begin_bar(open, high, low, close, bar_index)
if not na(fills.pending) and strat.position_quantity() > 0.0
    // Derive the exit from the entry price; continue_bar checks the rest of this bar.
    entryPrice = strat.position_avg_price()
    strat.exit("Trail", fromEntry = "Long", stop = entryPrice * 0.95, activateOnEntryBar = true, trailPrice = entryPrice * 1.05, trailOffset = entryPrice * 0.02)
strat.continue_bar(open, high, low, close)
if crossedUp and strat.position_quantity() == 0.0
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 10.0)
strat.end_bar(close, false)
```

entries.summary: Creates a coordinator that opens and closes independently accounted lots immediately, within the current bar.

parameters.name: broker
parameters.description: A broker with the [`broker.ImmediateBroker`](#broker.ImmediateBroker) methods, normally from [`broker.new`](#broker.new).

parameters.name: portfolio
parameters.description: A portfolio with the [`portfolio.LotLedger`](#portfolio.LotLedger) methods, normally from [`portfolio.lots`](#portfolio.lots).

entries.returns: A [`trade.LotTrade`](#trade.LotTrade) that owns both values.
entries.body:
Each bar, call `begin_bar(close, bar_index)`, then `entry`, `close_trade` or
`close_trade_at_stop`, then `mark()`. Each entry fill carries the `tradeId`
that later closes refer to.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

basis = ta.sma(close, 20)
crossedUp = ta.crossover(close, basis)
crossedDown = ta.crossunder(close, basis)

var strat = trade.lots(broker.new(), portfolio.lots(initialCash = 10000.0))
var int lotId = 0
var float lotStop = na
strat.begin_bar(close, bar_index)
if lotId > 0
    stopFill = strat.close_trade_at_stop("Stop", lotId, broker.Side.buy, open, high, low, lotStop)
    if not na(stopFill)
        lotId := 0
if lotId > 0 and crossedDown
    strat.close_trade("Exit", lotId)
    lotId := 0
if lotId == 0 and crossedUp
    entryFill = strat.entry("Long", "Cover", trade.Direction.long, notional = 1000.0)
    if not na(entryFill)
        lotId := entryFill.tradeId
        lotStop := close * 0.97
strat.mark()
```

Create it with [`trade.ohlc`](#trade.ohlc). It does not assume whether the high or
the low came first and has no trailing exits; use [`trade.PathTrade`](#trade.PathTrade)
when either matters. Each bar, call `begin_bar`, submit orders and exits,
then call `end_bar`. Use these methods rather than calling `broker` or
`portfolio` directly.

entries.summary: Coordinator that replays each bar as an ordered price path, with fixed and trailing exits.

rows: Broker that validates and fills this coordinator's orders.
Portfolio that records this coordinator's fills.
Bar index from the latest `begin_bar`, or `-1` before the first; later orders record it as `signalBarIndex`.
`broker.BarMatches begin_bar(float openPrice, float highPrice, float lowPrice, float closePrice, int barIndex)`

Starts a bar: fills the pending order along this bar's path and records where it filled. Market orders fill at the open; a stop entry fills at the open when the bar gaps past its stop, otherwise where the path crosses it. The attached exit is not checked here; `continue_bar` checks it on the rest of the path, so an exit derived from this fill can be attached first. `openPrice`: the bar's open. `highPrice`: the bar's high. `lowPrice`: the bar's low. `closePrice`: the bar's close. `barIndex`: the bar's index, normally `bar_index`. Returns: a [`broker.BarMatches`](#broker.BarMatches): `pending` holds the order's fill and `reversalClose` the closing fill when that order reversed the position, each `na` when absent; `exit` is always `na`.
`broker.Fill continue_bar(float openPrice, float highPrice, float lowPrice, float closePrice)`

Checks the attached exit, including its trailing stop, along the part of the bar after `begin_bar`'s fill. Call it after `begin_bar` and any exit changes, with the same prices. When nothing filled in `begin_bar`, it checks the whole bar. `openPrice`: the bar's open. `highPrice`: the bar's high. `lowPrice`: the bar's low. `closePrice`: the bar's close. Returns: the exit's fill, or `na` when the exit did not trigger.
`broker.Order entry(string commandId, Direction direction, float qty = na, Sizing sizing = na, float stop = na)`

Submits a market or stop entry order that fills in a later bar. Pass at most one of `qty` and `sizing` (both together are rejected); with neither, the broker sizes the entry from all available capital. An entry against the open position reverses it: the broker closes the position, then opens the new one. Adding to a position requires the same `commandId` and room under the portfolio's `pyramiding`. Resubmitting a pending stop entry with the same `commandId` and a new `stop` replaces it. `commandId`: name of the order; exits and `cancel` refer to it. `direction`: `trade.Direction.long` to buy or `trade.Direction.short` to sell. `qty`: quantity to open or add; must be positive. `sizing`: percent-of-equity sizing from [`trade.percentOfEquity`](#trade.percentOfEquity) or [`trade.percentOfEquityAtFill`](#trade.percentOfEquityAtFill). `stop`: stop price that makes this a stop entry: a long triggers at or above it, a short at or below it. Returns: the accepted [`broker.Order`](#broker.Order), or `na` when the broker rejects it on submission, for example while another order is pending.
`broker.Order exit(string commandId, string fromEntry, float stop = na, float target = na, bool activateOnEntryBar = false, float trailPrice = na, float trailOffset = na)`

Attaches a fixed and/or trailing exit that closes the whole position opened by entry `fromEntry`. Give any of `stop`, `target` and the trailing pair `trailPrice` with `trailOffset`; for a long the stop must be below the target, for a short above it. Once active, the trailing stop takes the place of `stop` whenever it is tighter. `fromEntry` must name the pending entry or the entry that opened the position. One exit is attached at a time: resubmitting the same `commandId` and `fromEntry` replaces it, and closing the position cancels it. `commandId`: name of the exit; `cancel` takes it. `fromEntry`: `commandId` of the entry the exit belongs to. `stop`: stop price. `target`: target price. `activateOnEntryBar`: whether the exit may fill on the bar its entry fills. `trailPrice`: price that activates the trailing stop. `trailOffset`: distance the trailing stop keeps from the best price reached since activation. Returns: the accepted order, or `na` when the broker rejects it on submission.

Submits an order that closes the whole position at the next open. The broker rejects it if the position is flat when it would fill. `commandId`: name of the order; `cancel` takes it. Returns: the accepted order, or `na` when the broker rejects it on submission.

Submits an order that moves the position to `target` at the next open. When it fills, the broker trades the difference between the target and the position, and cancels the order if there is none. Submitting again with the same `commandId` while it is pending replaces the target. `commandId`: name of the order; `cancel` takes it. `target`: target from [`trade.targetQuantity`](#trade.targetQuantity) or [`trade.targetPercentOfEquity`](#trade.targetPercentOfEquity). Returns: the accepted order, or `na` when the broker rejects it on submission.

Cancels the pending order or attached exit named `commandId`. Cancelling a pending entry also cancels an exit attached to it while no position is open. `commandId`: name the order was submitted with. Returns: the number of orders cancelled; `0` when none matched.

Ends the bar: marks the portfolio at `closePrice` and, on the last bar, expires pending orders. This family never fills orders at the close. Tea has no builtin that marks the last bar, so pass `false` unless the script knows it, for example from an input. `closePrice`: the bar's close. `isLast`: whether this is the last bar of the data. Returns: the orders expired on the last bar as a [`broker.FinishResult`](#broker.FinishResult), or `na` when `isLast` is `false`.
Returns the signed position: positive when long, negative when short, `0` when flat.
Returns the average entry price of the open position, or `na` when flat.
Returns the portfolio's metrics as one [`portfolio.PortfolioSnapshot`](#portfolio.PortfolioSnapshot). Its `equity` is from the latest `end_bar`.
Returns whether an order or attached exit is pending.
Returns whether the pending order is an entry.

entries.body:
Create it with [`trade.path`](#trade.path). The path runs from the open to the
nearer of the high and low, then to the farther one, then to the close;
when both are equally far, the low comes first. When an order fills partway
along the path, its exit only sees the rest of the bar. Each bar, call
`begin_bar`, attach or adjust exits, call `continue_bar`, submit new orders,
then call `end_bar`. Use these methods rather than calling `broker` or
`portfolio` directly.

entries.summary: Coordinator for independently accounted lots whose orders execute immediately, without waiting for a later bar.

rows: Broker that validates and executes this coordinator's orders.
Bar index from the latest `begin_bar`, or `-1` before the first; later orders record it as `signalBarIndex`.
Close captured by the latest `begin_bar`; `entry`, `close_trade` and `mark` use it as their price.
Starts a bar by recording the close and bar index that later calls in the bar use. `closePrice`: the bar's close. `barIndex`: the bar's index, normally `bar_index`. Returns: `barIndex`.
`broker.Fill entry(string commandId, string reversalCommandId, Direction direction, float qty = na, float notional = na)`

Opens a new lot at the captured close, first closing every lot on the opposite side. Give exactly one of `qty` and `notional`, positive; otherwise the entry is rejected before anything closes. If an opposite lot fails to close, the entry is skipped. The broker rejects entries beyond the portfolio's `maxOpenTrades`. `commandId`: name of the entry order. `reversalCommandId`: name of the orders that close opposite lots. `direction`: side of the new lot. `qty`: quantity of the new lot. `notional`: value of the new lot; the broker converts it to a quantity at the fill price. Returns: the entry's fill, whose `tradeId` identifies the new lot, or `na` when no lot opened.

Closes the open lot `tradeId` now, at the captured close. The close is rejected when no open lot has that id. `commandId`: name of the closing order. `tradeId`: trade id of the lot, from its entry fill. Returns: the closing fill, or `na` when the close was rejected.
`broker.Fill close_trade_at_stop(string commandId, int tradeId, broker.Side entrySide, float openPrice, float highPrice, float lowPrice, float stopPrice)`

Closes lot `tradeId` if this bar reached `stopPrice`; the broker decides the fill price. A long lot's stop is reached when the low is at or below it, a short lot's when the high is at or above it. The fill is based on the open when the bar gapped past the stop, otherwise on the stop. If the stop was not reached, nothing happens; if it was, the close is rejected when the lot is missing or was not opened on `entrySide`. `commandId`: name of the closing order. `tradeId`: trade id of the lot, from its entry fill. `entrySide`: side the lot was opened on: `broker.Side.buy` for a long lot, `broker.Side.sell` for a short one. `openPrice`: the bar's open. `highPrice`: the bar's high. `lowPrice`: the bar's low. `stopPrice`: the lot's stop level. Returns: the closing fill, or `na` when the stop was not reached or the close was rejected.
Values the lots at the close captured by `begin_bar`, updating equity, peak equity and drawdown. Returns: the new equity.
Returns the signed total of the open lots: positive when long, negative when short.
Returns the average entry price of the open lots, or `na` when none are open.
Returns the portfolio's metrics as one [`portfolio.PortfolioSnapshot`](#portfolio.PortfolioSnapshot). Its `equity` is from the latest `mark`.

entries.body:
Create it with [`trade.lots`](#trade.lots). `entry` and `close_trade` execute at the
close captured by `begin_bar`; `close_trade_at_stop` executes when the bar
reached the stop. Each entry opens a lot with its own trade id. Each bar,
call `begin_bar`, then entries and closes, then `mark`. Keep per-lot exit
rules, such as stops, in your own state keyed by the trade id. Use these
methods rather than calling `broker` or `portfolio` directly.

pages.title: broker
pages.description: Order and fill types, and a deterministic broker emulator that fills strategy orders against bar prices.
pages.intro:
Order and fill types, and a deterministic broker emulator that fills strategy orders against bar prices.

A broker turns strategy commands into orders, decides whether, when and at
what price each order fills, applies commission and slippage, and reports
each step as an event. The portfolio library applies fills to cash and
positions, and a trade coordinator sequences broker and portfolio on every
bar. A strategy imports all three, creates a broker with [`broker.new`](#broker.new)
or [`broker.basic`](#broker.basic), and hands it with a portfolio to a coordinator such
as [`trade.nextOpen`](#trade.nextOpen); it then trades through the coordinator rather
than calling the broker. See the strategy model for the full
responsibility boundary and the
backtest guide for a runnable
walkthrough.

The library keeps no global state: each broker value holds its own orders,
ids and matching state. Broker events are appended to one output per event
type, such as `broker.FillExecuted`; each output keeps execution order, but
separate outputs share no ordering.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

fast = ta.ema(close, 10)
slow = ta.ema(close, 30)

var strat = trade.nextOpen(
    broker.new(commission = broker.commissionRate(0.001)),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 10000.0)
)

strat.begin_bar(open, bar_index)
if ta.crossover(fast, slow)
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long)
if ta.crossunder(fast, slow)
    strat.close("Long")
strat.end_bar(close, false)

metrics = strat.snapshot()
plot("equity", metrics.equity, "equity")
```

Add `import broker` to a script to use these as `broker.name`.

parameters.description: commission as a fraction of notional

entries.returns: a `rate` [`broker.Commission`](#broker.Commission).
entries.body:
`0.001` charges 0.1%. A negative or `na` rate makes the broker reject every
fill with `invalidConfiguration`.

parameters.name: cash

parameters.name: rate
parameters.description: slippage as a fraction of price

entries.returns: a `rate` [`broker.Slippage`](#broker.Slippage).
entries.body:
`0.001` fills buys 0.1% above and sells 0.1% below the matched price. The
rate must be at least `0` and below `1`; otherwise the broker rejects every
fill with `invalidConfiguration`.

entries.summary: Adverse slippage as a percent of the matched price.

parameters.name: percent
parameters.description: slippage as a percent of price

entries.returns: a `rate` [`broker.Slippage`](#broker.Slippage) holding `percent / 100`.
entries.body:
`0.1` moves each fill 0.1% against the order; the same as
`slippageRate(percent / 100)`.

entries.summary: Adverse slippage as a number of price ticks.

parameters.name: ticks
parameters.description: number of ticks per fill

parameters.name: tickSize
parameters.description: price size of one tick

entries.returns: a `ticks` [`broker.Slippage`](#broker.Slippage).
entries.body:
Buys fill `ticks * tickSize` above the matched price and sells the same
distance below. Neither may be negative, and `tickSize` must be positive
whenever `ticks` is not zero; otherwise the broker rejects every fill with
`invalidConfiguration`.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

// Two ticks of 0.25 against every fill, plus 2.5 per contract.
var strat = trade.nextOpen(
    broker.new(
        commission = broker.commissionCashPerContract(2.5),
        slippage = broker.slippageTicks(2.0, 0.25)
    ),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 50000.0)
)
```

signatures:
broker.new(
    Commission commission = Commission.new(CommissionKind.rate, 0.0),
    Slippage slippage = Slippage.new(SlippageKind.rate, 0.0, 0.0),
    bool processOrdersOnClose = false,
)

parameters.name: commission
parameters.description: commission setting from a helper such as [`broker.commissionRate`](#broker.commissionRate)

parameters.name: slippage
parameters.description: adverse slippage setting from a helper such as [`broker.slippageTicks`](#broker.slippageTicks)

parameters.name: processOrdersOnClose
parameters.description: whether pending commands may also fill at bar closes

entries.returns: a new [`broker.BrokerEmulator`](#broker.BrokerEmulator).
entries.body:
With the defaults it charges no commission or slippage. With
`processOrdersOnClose = true`, the next-open and OHLC coordinators also fill
pending commands at bar closes, including the close of the bar a command was
issued on. Pass the result to a trade coordinator such as
[`trade.nextOpen`](#trade.nextOpen).

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

var strat = trade.ohlc(
    broker.new(
        commission = broker.commissionPercent(0.05),
        slippage = broker.slippageTicks(1.0, 0.01),
        processOrdersOnClose = true
    ),
    portfolio.new(initialCash = 10000.0)
)

average = ta.sma(close, 20)
strat.begin_bar(open, high, low, bar_index)
if ta.crossover(close, average)
    // Fills at this bar's close because processOrdersOnClose is true.
    strat.entry("Long", trade.Direction.long, qty = 10.0)
strat.end_bar(close, false)
```

parameters.name: adverseSlippageRate
parameters.description: slippage as a fraction of price, as in [`broker.slippageRate`](#broker.slippageRate)

parameters.name: takerFeeRate
parameters.description: commission as a fraction of notional, as in [`broker.commissionRate`](#broker.commissionRate)

entries.body:
The same as [`broker.new`](#broker.new) with
`commission = broker.commissionRate(takerFeeRate)`,
`slippage = broker.slippageRate(adverseSlippageRate)` and
`processOrdersOnClose = false`. Note the argument order: slippage first,
then the fee.

```tea
import broker
import portfolio
import trade

// 0.05% adverse slippage, then a 0.1% commission.
var strat = trade.nextOpen(broker.basic(0.0005, 0.001), portfolio.new())
```

position. With long margin enabled, a buy from a flat or long position is
limited to what the buying power pays for, so the position can stop short of
the target. A difference below `0.0000001` cancels the order instead.

The broker validates it when it is submitted or executed, and turns it into
an [`broker.Order`](#broker.Order). Which fields apply depends on `kind`; the rest keep
their defaults, and prices are absolute levels. An entry uses at most one of
`quantity`, `notional`, `cashBudget` and `equityPercent`; with none set, a
scheduled entry spends all available capital, cash for a buy and equity for
a sell.

place on the path is recorded so `match_path_exit` continues from there.

the entry fill unless `activateOnEntryBar` is set. A gap past the stop
or target fills at the open; otherwise a touched level fills at that
level, and when both are touched, the side whose extreme is nearer the
open wins, ties going to the stop. A triggered exit is removed even if
its fill is rejected, and outside `match_path_exit` a trailing exit is
rejected and removed. Tick slippage cannot take the exit price below one
tick. Called by `begin_bar` of [`trade.OhlcTrade`](#trade.OhlcTrade). `openPrice`: the bar's open. `highPrice`: the bar's high. `lowPrice`: the bar's low. `account`: account view from the portfolio. `barIndex`: current bar index. Returns: the exit fill, or `na`.

favor advance it. `fromPrice`: segment start price. `toPrice`: segment end price. `account`: account view from the portfolio. `barIndex`: current bar index. Returns: `0`.

Matches the attached exit on one path segment, then updates the trailing stop if nothing filled. A trailing stop moved by a segment applies from the next segment. `fromPrice`: segment start price. `toPrice`: segment end price. `account`: account view from the portfolio. `barIndex`: current bar index. Matches the attached exit along the rest of the bar's path, segment by segment. It starts where the pending command filled on this bar, or at the open,
so earlier prices on the bar cannot trigger the exit; trailing stops
activate and ratchet as the path advances. Called by `continue_bar` of
[`trade.PathTrade`](#trade.PathTrade). `openPrice`: the bar's open. `highPrice`: the bar's high. `lowPrice`: the bar's low. `closePrice`: the bar's close. `account`: account view from the portfolio. `barIndex`: current bar index. Returns: the exit fill, or `na`.
